what: a time read or named on the picture alone counted from the picture's first frame where a cut counts from the file's start: FFmpeg counts an MPEG-TS/PS decode of the picture without the sound from the picture's own start (6.1.1), and -start_at_zero does too. On a .ts whose sound leads its picture by 21 ms, at 25 fps, look.py --at 2.5 showed frame 63 where cut.py --start 2.5 starts on 62; with a 0.3 s lead look.py --at, --compare, the contact sheet and the review page's stills were 8 frames late (an .mpg still 18), scenes.py put its cut (and so metadata.py --auto-chapters --from scenes) 0.33 s early, the analysis windows (cropdetect, --motion-centre, fit's crop check, scenes --shots) sat on the picture's clock, and check.py --levels put its worst frame 0.32 s early on every container, MP4 included, by subtracting the picture's first frame time
escaped: #696's TimestampSeekTests picked their reference frame with a select on a video-only decode, FFmpeg's picture clock, the same clock as the grab, so the grab agreed with it and the 21 ms difference was written down as seen; #787's guard looked at sound-only reads, and every picture-only read was taken to be on the file's clock because MP4 and Matroska put a late picture there, which every other fixture used
mechanism: decision.picture_seek(meta, at, ..., seconds) is the one decode of the picture from a time: -copyts, the input seek seek_margin() early, and setpts=PTS-<start_time>/TB with a trim at the head of the chain; look.py, _review.still, probe.seek_args (cropdetect, fit, scenes --shots, loop), probe.detect_scenes with scenes.py --sheet, and probe.measure_signal_range call it. The guard test_guards.TimeGuard.test_a_picture_read_alone_counts_from_the_files_start makes one take as .mp4, .ts and .mpg with its picture 0.3 s after its sound and fails wherever look --at, the review still, scenes.py's cut or check.py --levels' worst frame is not the frame the file's own clock has there; TimestampSeekTests now picks its reference frame on the file's clock
